abstract: Purpose Radical periarterial techniques, including artery-first approaches, mesopancreas excision, arterial resection, periarterial divestment and the TRIANGLE operation, address the same periarterial compartment under different names, and their literature has not been mapped as a whole. This study aimed to map the growth, contributors, collaboration patterns, thematic evolution and randomized evidence of this field. Methods The Web of Science Core Collection was searched on 6 October 2026 for English-language articles and reviews. After title and abstract screening, 539 records were analysed. Performance indicators were calculated, and co-authorship and keyword co-occurrence networks were built with VOSviewer. Reporting followed the BIBLIO guideline. Results The 539 documents (2000–2026) appeared in 128 journals and received 13,491 citations (h-index 56). Annual output grew by 14.4% per year between 2010 and 2025. Japan contributed the most documents (n = 161) but had the lowest international collaboration rate among the leading countries (2.1%). Heidelberg University was the most productive and most cited institution. The co-authorship network comprised 11 clusters, led by Japanese groups and a Heidelberg-centred European group. Arterial divestment, conversion surgery, robotic surgery and the TRIANGLE operation were among the newest themes. Only three completed randomized controlled trials were identified, all testing artery-first approaches; none addressed the TRIANGLE operation, divestment or arterial resection. Conclusion Research on radical periarterial pancreatic surgery has moved from extended en bloc resection to neoadjuvant-enabled, artery-preserving clearance, yet these operations rest almost entirely on non-randomized evidence. Standardized definitions of periarterial clearance and multinational randomized trials are needed.
